newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy refuses asylum to Albanian refugees.
newsitem.headline: Italy refuses asylum to Albanian refugees.

text.p: Italy said on Saturday it was turning down asylum requests from Albanian refugees fleeing unrest in the south of their country and would send them back.

"Although we understand their fear of being caught up in the disorder in the south...the government does not consider that the public order situation in the rest of the country presents conditions of emergency or other risks for personal safety," the interior and foreign affairs ministries said in a statement.
The joint statement said the Italian government "noted with preoccupation continual arrivals...of Albanian citizens largely coming from Vlore and nearby regions".

Refugees without legal entry papers will be sent back to Durres, a port near Tirana, and then on to the capital. The statement said Italy was prepared to set up a centre in Durres, possibly staffed by Italian humanitarian and government officials, to assist the repatriation effort.
The government was also studying sending urgent supplies and humaitarian aid to the south of Albania, in agreement with the Albanian authorities via the Red Cross.

Seventy Albanians crossed from Vlore on Friday. Italy tried to repatriate 46 of them but failed when the Albanians refused to board the ferry and asked for political asylum. Italy earlier on Saturday evacuated 33 Italians and Albanians from Vlore.
